fields.latestPosition: VWG – low priority; requires a shutdown to implement.
fields.why: PLC logic cycles through each Modbus client for about one second to read health status. On Prosoft modules with 11 clients, a comms loss can go undetected for about 10 seconds, and a return to healthy takes as long to confirm.
fields.design:
- Update Prosoft configurations to map client status/error into spare Modbus addressing so health is monitored continuously
- Replace Modbus health statuses where appropriate and alarm when Modbus is unhealthy – high priority for control devices, low for monitoring-only devices
- Ensure adequate timeouts (typically 2 s)
- New SCADA page/faceplate, accessible from the PLC page: total requests, responses, errors, configuration error word, current error, last error
fields.impact: CROs will see Modbus comms alarms prioritised by device criticality, plus a new Modbus diagnostics faceplate.
fields.scheduleNote: Low priority; requires a shutdown to implement (VWG).
